title: Classification of Indian Mineral Resources
subject: Geography
description: A classification diagram illustrating the major metallic and non-metallic mineral resources found in India, detailing their primary producing states and key industrial applications.
mermaidCode: graph TD A[Indian Mineral Resources] --> B{Category} B --> C[Metallic Minerals] B --> D[Non-Metallic Minerals] C --> C1[Iron Ore] C1 --> C1a(Odisha, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, MP) C1 --> C1b(Steel industry, ferro-alloys) C --> C2[Bauxite] C2 --> C2a(Odisha, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Jharkhand) C2 --> C2b(Aluminium production, refractory bricks) C --> C3[Copper] C3 --> C3a(Rajasthan, Jharkhand, MP) C3 --> C3b(Electrical wiring, alloy production) C --> C4[Zinc] C4 --> C4a(Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Jharkhand) C4 --> C4b(Galvanisation, die-casting) C --> C5[Gold] C5 --> C5a(Karnataka, Jharkhand, Rajasthan) C5 --> C5b(Jewellery, electronics, reserves) C --> C6[Uranium] C6 --> C6a(Rajasthan, MP, Tamil Nadu) C6 --> C6b(Nuclear power programme) D --> D1[Coal] D1 --> D1a(Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, WB) D1 --> D1b(Power generation, steel making, cement) D --> D2[Mica] D2 --> D2a(Jharkhand, MP, Rajasthan) D2 --> D2b(Electronics, insulation, cosmetics) D --> D3[Limestone] D3 --> D3a(Rajasthan, MP, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka) D3 --> D3b(Cement, steel, glass)
